name: Courier engine protocol
doc: How Courier.app talks to its courier-engine helper. This file is the single definition: the engine's Go tests and the app's Swift tests both check the examples in examples/ against it, and the Swift Codable types are named exactly as the entries in types. Copyright 2026 VitruvianSoftware, SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later.

transport.socket: A Unix stream socket at <data dir>/engine.sock, mode 0600, in a 0700 directory. Nothing listens on TCP.
transport.framing: JSON-RPC 2.0. Each message is one UTF-8 JSON object on one line, ended by a single \n. A line is at most max_frame_bytes bytes, not counting the \n.
transport.oversize: A line longer than max_frame_bytes closes the connection. Nothing is answered.
transport.requests: Every request has "jsonrpc": "2.0", an "id" (a string or a number, echoed in the answer), a "method", and "params" (an object; it may be left out when the method takes none). A key in params that the method does not take is -32602, and data.reason names it ("unknown parameter replyTo"). A message with no id is a notification; the engine defines none from the client, so it is ignored and not answered. A batch (a JSON array) is -32600.
transport.concurrency: Requests are answered as they finish, not in the order sent: some (message.send, login.wait) wait for a network. Match answers to requests by id. Notifications can arrive between any two answers.
transport.closing: Closing the connection cancels everything it has in flight. A login.wait in flight is cancelled, and so is its sign-in.

conventions.doc: Numbers both sides keep to; the engine's Go tests and the app's Swift tests both read them from here, so the two sides cannot drift. typing_repeat_ms: while the text in the composer keeps changing, the app sends room.setTyping true at the first change and again every typing_repeat_ms, and false when the person stops (5 s after the last change), sends, clears the box or leaves the chat. The bridges hand a start to the network only once, and the networks time a start out (Telegram after about 5 s), so the engine turns a pulse that comes 3 s or more after its last start (a second short of typing_repeat_ms, so a pulse a little early still counts) into a stop and a start, and the other side keeps seeing it.

handshake.doc: The first request on a connection must be hello. Any other method before a successful hello is -32002. A hello with a different protocol number is -32001 with data {"engine": <the engine's protocol>}, and the app shows "update needed". Once a hello has succeeded, the connection receives a changed notification for every change from when it answered on, the first of them after hello's answer. hello may be sent again: with the engine's protocol it answers the same; with another it is -32001; either way the connection stays as it was, greeted, with one feed.

type_grammar.int: a JSON number with no fraction
type_grammar.object: any JSON object; its keys are not part of this protocol (an event's Matrix content)
type_grammar.map<T>: a JSON object whose values are all T
type_grammar.T|null: the key is always there; the value is T or null
type_grammar.T?: the key may be left out; when it is there the value is T
type_grammar.Name: a type defined in types
type_grammar.values: a field with values only ever holds one of them
type_grammar.times: Every time (ts, last_ts, due_at) is Unix milliseconds.
type_grammar.durations: Every *_ms that is not a time is a length of time in milliseconds.
type_grammar.paths: Every *_path is an absolute path on this Mac, or "" when there is no such file.

Empty.doc: No params, or a result with nothing in it.

protocol.doc: The protocol the app speaks. This file's protocol.
The protocol the engine speaks: the same as the app's.

networks.doc: The network names the engine knows, in display order: the order of accounts.list.

Account.doc: One network the engine knows, linked or not.

network.doc: The network's name: whatsapp, signal, telegram, slack, gmessages.

display_name.doc: The network's name for people: WhatsApp.

flows.doc: The sign-in flows it offers, preferred first. The value to pass to login.start.

state.doc: The account's state, summed up over its logins: the first login that needs the person (LOGGED_OUT, BAD_CREDENTIALS, UNKNOWN_ERROR), else the first one reconnecting (CONNECTING, TRANSIENT_DISCONNECT, BRIDGE_UNREACHABLE), else the first; with no login, the bridge's own state_event, or UNCONFIGURED when it is running and has said nothing yet. STARTING: the engine hasn't started the network yet this session and will; its chats are listed and open, a message sent in one waits, there is no banner and no Add a Network prompt, and a sign-in on it is -32016 until it runs. NOT_STARTED: the engine could not start it (not_started says why).

error.doc: What went wrong, for people: the bridge's message, or its error code when it gave no message, for the login state sums up. "" when nothing is wrong.

remote_name.doc: What the network calls the linked account: the first login's. "" when none is linked.

not_started.doc: Why the engine did not start the network (Telegram without its api_id and api_hash, say). "" unless state is NOT_STARTED.

syncs.doc: The chat changes Courier also sends to this network, so they show on the phone too. Every other change (archive, low priority, hide, labels, reminders, drafts, unread marks) stays on this Mac, and so does everything when the list is empty: the network isn't running or has no account. Sending is best effort: a network that is offline or refuses keeps the change on this Mac only.

can_create_group.doc: Whether any linked account on this network can create group chats (its bridge client implements GroupCreatingNetworkAPI). False when the network isn't running or has no account.

logins.doc: Each account signed in on the network (a network can hold more than one: a second phone number, a second workspace), in account_id order, the first being the one login.start signs in again when it is given neither another nor account_id. An account the bridge no longer has is left out. [] when none is linked. While the network isn't running (STARTING, NOT_STARTED) each is listed as the engine last knew it, with the account's state and no error.

Login.doc: One account signed in on a network: what Reconnect and the banners name when the network has more than one. Login here, and login_name on an inbox row, mean an account (account_id); login_id everywhere in this protocol means a sign-in session (LoginStep, login.submit, login.wait, login.cancel), never an account.

account_id.doc: The account's ID on its network, as the bridge keeps it: what login.start's account_id takes to sign it in again. Not a sign-in's login_id.

remote_name.doc: What the network calls the account (a phone number, a workspace's name). "" when it hasn't said.

state.doc: This account's own state, as Account.state's values.

error.doc: What went wrong with this account, for people: the bridge's message, or its error code. "" when nothing is wrong.

can_create_group.doc: Whether this account's bridge client implements GroupCreatingNetworkAPI and can create group chats. False while the network isn't running.

accounts.doc: One per network, in the order of hello's networks.

last_ts.doc: When its newest message was sent. 0 when it has none yet.

preview.doc: The newest message's text, at most 140 characters. "" when there is nothing readable.

preview_kind.doc: What the newest message is. For a poll, preview is its question. timer_change: a note that the chat's disappearing timer changed (a bridge's, or one the engine wrote for a change made in Courier); preview is "", and the app words it. call: a bridge's notice of a call; preview is "", preview_call says what happened, and the app words it.

preview_status.doc: How far the newest message has got, when it is mine and has gone (not a note): seen (someone has read it or anything after it), else delivered (someone's device has it; the networks report this in one-to-one chats only), else sent. "" for anything else: someone else's message, one of mine not sent yet (queued, waiting, pending, failed), a note, or no message.

login_name.doc: The name of the account the chat is on (its Login's remote_name), for a small tag on the row: an account, not a sign-in session's login_id. "" unless the network has more than one account (Account.logins) and the chat is one account's own: a chat every account of the network shares (a WhatsApp group) has none.

unread.doc: Messages from others after the read marker.

pinned.doc: Pinned chats come first in every sort, in the order they were pinned.

marked_unread.doc: Marked unread by me (or by a reminder that fired), whatever unread says.

request.doc: A message request: someone new writing first, waiting for room.acceptRequest.

draft.doc: The unsent text of the chat's composer, whole. "" when there is none.

labels.doc: The label_id of each label on the chat, smallest first.

muted_by.doc: What else mutes the chat: its account's space, or one of its labels' spaces. "" when nothing does. An account mute wins.

muted_by_name.doc: For muted_by account, the network's display name (WhatsApp); for label, the title of the first muted label, by label_id. "" otherwise.

reminder.doc: The chat's reminder, set or fired. null when it has none.

typing.doc: Who is typing in the chat now, by name: their name in the chat, else their profile's, else their ID's localpart. In order of their IDs.

unread_mentions.doc: The unread messages that mention me, by name or the whole chat.

preview_media_path.doc: When the newest message is an image or a sticker: its thumbnail (or the image itself), when the engine has it. "" otherwise.

preview_call.doc: For a preview_kind of call, what happened; null for any other.

remote_name.doc: The chat's name on its network, before any local override.

local_name.doc: The name set on this Mac (Just for Me), or "".

local_avatar_path.doc: The picture set on this Mac (Just for Me), or "".

merge_id.doc: The merged chat this room belongs to, or "".

CallNote.doc: A bridge's notice of a call, as Courier reads it. An event's content carries the same object as fi.courier.call when it is a call notice (com.beeper.action_message of type call); a call notice without it rang. Whether it was mine is the event's (or the row's preview_mine).

state.doc: ringing: a call came in (mine: I called). started: a group's call started. missed: no one answered. ended: it is over (answered, except on Signal, which doesn't say). declined: it was turned down. dropped: the connection was lost.

Reminder.doc: Bring a chat back to my attention at due_at. When it fires the chat is marked unread and comes back from the archive, and the engine sends changed kind reminder. Reading the chat ends a fired reminder.

condition.doc: if_no_reply: only if I haven't sent a message in the chat since setting it; otherwise it just ends. always: whatever happens.

InboxListParams.doc: One page of chats. Leave everything out for the first page of the inbox, newest first. Or give room_ids alone to look those chats up wherever they are (after a changed notification, say).

space.doc: A space_id from spaces.list. Left out means inbox.

filters.doc: Left out or [] is All. Filters of one group are or'ed and the groups and'ed: dms with groups; unanswered with no_reply; the places archived, low_priority, hidden, requests, reminders and send_later, which take the space's place (its account or label still applies). unread, drafts, unknown (a one-to-one chat with no name, or a phone number for a name) and muted each stand alone. There is no all filter.

sort.doc: By the newest message (chats with none by when they arrived), or by reminder time, chats without one last. Left out means newest.

cursor.doc: The last page's next_cursor, for the page after it. Only the query that handed it out takes it (the same space, filters, sort and room_ids); any other cursor is -32602. limit may change between pages.

limit.doc: 1 to 500. 200 when left out. A page holds at most this many chats, and fewer when that many would pass 1 MiB (long drafts): next_cursor says there is more.

room_ids.doc: 1 to 100 chats to look up, in any space or place, archived or hidden. Not with space, filters or sort. A room_id the engine doesn't have is left out.

next_cursor.doc: Pass as cursor for the next page. null on the last page.

Space.doc: One entry of the spaces bar.

space_id.doc: inbox, reminders, requests, low_priority, send_later, archive, account:<network> or label:<label_id>. Pass it to inbox.list as space.

title.doc: An account's network display name (WhatsApp) or a label's title. "" for a built-in space: the app names those.

network.doc: For an account, its network. "" otherwise.

color.doc: For a label: an index into the app's list of system colours, 0 to 11. 0 otherwise.

icon.doc: For a label: an SF Symbol name. "" otherwise.

muted.doc: For an account or a label: its chats are muted (spaces.update). false for a built-in space.

show_in_inbox.doc: For an account or a label: which of its chats also show in the inbox space. "" for a built-in space.

chats.doc: How many chats inbox.list lists for this space.

unread_chats.doc: How many of them are unread.

attention_chats.doc: For inbox: how many of its unread chats (unread, or marked unread) nothing mutes, neither the chat itself, its account nor a label. It is the Dock badge and the menu bar's count, so it doesn't change with the space or filters the app shows. 0 for every other space.

spaces.doc: In the bar's order, hidden ones in their place. inbox is always first. The built-in spaces, an account per network with an account, and every label: a space the saved layout doesn't name yet goes at the end.

order.doc: space_ids in the bar's order, each once, starting with inbox.

hidden.doc: The space_ids in order to hide. Not inbox.

title.doc: 1 to 40 characters, once spaces at either end are trimmed.

icon.doc: An SF Symbol name, at most 64 bytes.

LabelUpdateParams.doc: A field left out stays as it is.

mark_read.doc: Also mark read each chat this archived (or unarchived).

room_ids.doc: The chats that changed, in the order asked for; [] when none did.

on.doc: true puts the label on, false takes it off.

text.doc: At most 16,384 characters. "" clears the draft.

due_at.doc: After now and at most 5 years ahead.

archive.doc: Also archive the chats, all but pinned ones, until the reminder brings them back.

space.doc: inbox (when left out), an account:<network> or a label:<label_id>. Only the chats it lists with no place filter count, and never a pinned one.

read_only.doc: Only chats with nothing unread and not marked unread.

older_than_ms.doc: Only chats whose newest message (or, with none, whose arrival) is older than this: 0 (any age) or 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 or 365 days.

dry_run.doc: Say which chats, and change nothing.

space.doc: A space_id. Left out means inbox.

AutoArchiveRule.doc: A rule that archives chats by itself. The General setting is one after_reply or after_read rule with scope all; each space can have one older_than rule.

rule_id.doc: 0 in autoArchive.set makes a new rule.

scope.doc: all, or for an older_than rule the space it sweeps: account:<network> or label:<label_id> (all sweeps the inbox).

trigger.doc: after_reply: duration_ms after I send a message. after_read: duration_ms after I read the chat. older_than: once the chat's newest message is older than duration_ms.

chat_type.doc: read: only chats with nothing unread and not marked unread.

duration_ms.doc: after_reply and after_read: 0, 1, 5, 10 or 30 minutes, 1 or 4 hours, 1 or 7 days. older_than: 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 or 365 days.

Cursor.doc: A place in a chat's history: one event's ts and seq. A page's before is its oldest event, and its after its newest.

RoomEventsParams.doc: Give at most one of before, after and around (more is -32602). None of them is the newest page.

merge_id.doc: A merged chat's merge_id: interleaves the events of its rooms.

thread.doc: A thread's root, an event_id in this chat: that thread's events only, newest first, paged with before. around or after with thread is -32602. A page holds the thread's replies and what the chat carries for them (their edits, their reactions and the redactions that delete them); the oldest page ends with the root itself and what it carries. Without thread, a reply that stays in its thread is left out (one also sent to the channel stays). A reply that carries more than a page holds (over 1 MiB) carries what fits, in this order: the redactions that delete it and its edits, then its reactions, each newest first. So its reactions are cut first, and its edits and redactions only if they alone pass 1 MiB. A root that isn't in this chat is -32020.

before.doc: A page's before, for the page older than it.

after.doc: A page's after, for the page newer than it.

around.doc: An event_id in this chat: the page with that event in the middle, about half of the rest older and half newer (an even limit leans newer). Near either end of the history the other side fills the page. A reply that stays in its thread (a search hit can be one) centres the page on its thread's root instead, when the chat has it; open the thread at the reply. An event that isn't in this chat is -32020.

Event.doc: One event in a chat: a message, a poll, a reaction, an edit or a redaction. A message deleted for me is left out of every page.

sender.doc: The sender's Matrix ID. @me:courier.local is me.

sender_name.doc: The sender's display name, or the localpart of their ID when they have none.

type.doc: The Matrix event type: m.room.message, m.reaction, m.sticker, m.room.redaction, m.room.encrypted, org.matrix.msc3381.poll.start (and its votes and end).

content.doc: The Matrix event content, as the bridge wrote it.

seq.doc: Arrival order in the engine. Breaks ties between equal ts.

status.doc: queued: held for undo send; message.undo takes it back, and it goes when its window ends (or with message.sendHeld). waiting: its network is starting, down or logging in (or messages typed before it in the chat are waiting); it goes, oldest first with the chat's other waiting messages, when the chat's account is back, however long that takes, and message.undo takes it back (Don't Send). pending while the network has not answered, sent, or failed (message.retry or message.discard).

status_reason.doc: Why it failed, for people. "" otherwise. Exactly "may have been sent" when the engine stopped while the message was pending: the network may have taken it. Exactly "not sent" for a held message whose window ended over an hour before the engine could send it, a held or scheduled one whose sending a quit cut short and that is over an hour late when Courier opens again, or a blast message that failed before reaching the network (for example, invalid text or an unknown room): nothing was sent. Exactly "not connected" for a held, scheduled or blast message whose network wasn't connected when it was due: nothing was sent. Exactly "network_refused" when the network refused a blast message. For a waiting message, exactly "no account" when none of my accounts is in the chat any more (the only one that was has been signed out, so a group every account shares has no account to go through): it can't go until one is, so the app says so rather than "Waiting to send", and Don't Send still takes it back; "" while it is just waiting. The app words these itself.

media_path.doc: The file the content's url names, when the engine has it, or "".

bookmarked.doc: I bookmarked it, on this Mac.

poll.doc: For a poll (org.matrix.msc3381.poll.start): how it stands. null for anything else.

thread.doc: For a thread's root: its replies. null when it has none.

expires_at.doc: When its after_send disappearing timer takes it. 0 is never. The app hides one past its time even before the engine deletes it.

delivered.doc: Someone's device has it. Only my messages that have gone; the networks report this in one-to-one chats only. false on others' messages.

read_by.doc: Who has read it or anything after it, newest receipt first, at most 50 (the newest): the app shows one name and a count. Only my messages that have gone (not a note); my own reads on other devices never count. [] on others' messages and on mine not sent yet.

thumbnail_path.doc: Local file path of the media thumbnail when available.

duration_ms.doc: Duration in milliseconds for audio, voice notes, and video.

is_gif.doc: Whether the media item is a GIF (content["fi.mau.gif"] or image/gif).

is_animated.doc: Whether the sticker or image is animated (GIF, APNG, or video/webm sticker).

view_once.doc: Whether the media item is view-once (an after_read disappearing timer that differs from the chat's timer and matches the bridge's view-once duration: 5 min on Signal, 15 s on Telegram).

link_previews.doc: Beeper link previews attached to the message.

played.doc: Whether this voice note or view-once item has been marked played on this Mac.

LinkPreviewItem.doc: One URL preview attached to a message (com.beeper.linkpreviews).

Reader.doc: Someone who has read a message of mine, or anything after it.

name.doc: As typing names people: their name in the chat, else their profile's, else their ID's localpart. Someone the chat doesn't list (its members can arrive later than a receipt) is named by their ID's localpart.

ts.doc: When their receipt says they read it. 0 when the receipt had no time.

PollTally.doc: A poll as it stands. Each person's newest vote counts, for options the poll has, at most max_selections of them; a vote after the poll ended doesn't.

max_selections.doc: How many options one person may choose: 1, or every option.

mine.doc: The ids of the options I chose. [] when I didn't vote.

ended.doc: Its creator ended it. No more votes count.

ThreadSummary.doc: What a thread's root shows. A deleted reply, or one that failed to send, doesn't count.

last_ts.doc: When the newest reply was sent.

last_senders.doc: Who wrote the newest replies, by name, newest first: at most 3 people.

events.doc: Newest first. A page may hold fewer than limit events, even none, to stay under 1 MiB or because messages deleted for me are left out: only before and after say whether there is more.

before.doc: Pass as before for the next, older page. null when there is no older event.

after.doc: The newest event of this page, to pass as after for the next newer page. null when the page has the chat's newest event, and always for a thread's page.

SearchParams.doc: One search, over every chat in any place. Empty text with no filters answers only last_archived and, when bookmarks is asked for, the five newest bookmarks; text of only emoji or punctuation runs nothing (hint emoji_only). Bookmarks, messages and media need 2 letters of text (or one character of a script written without spaces, such as 東); chats and people are found from the first letter.

text.doc: What was typed: 0 to 500 characters (Unicode scalars); longer is -32602. Quotes make a phrase, and the last word matches as a prefix while it is being typed. Emoji and punctuation separate words and are not searched.

sections.doc: What to search. Left out or [] is all five.

cursor.doc: The next_cursor of a page of bookmarks, media or messages, for the page after it. It needs sections to be exactly ["bookmarks"], ["media"] or ["messages"], and the same text and filters as the query that handed it out; any other is -32602. limit may change between pages.

limit.doc: Each section's most results. Left out, chats, in_groups and bookmarks take 5, media 12 and messages 20. Given, it is 1 to 100 when only chats and in_groups are asked for, and 1 to 50 otherwise.

open_room_id.doc: The chat open now, which last_archived leaves out.

SearchFilters.doc: Every filter narrows; filters together are and'ed. room_ids leaves out chats and in_groups. sender, kinds, since, until and partial narrow bookmarks, media and messages only; networks and chat_type narrow every section.

room_ids.doc: 1 to 100 chats to search in. A chat the engine doesn't have is -32020.

networks.doc: Network names, as hello lists them. One the engine doesn't know is -32602.

kinds.doc: Any of these. A link is a text message holding an http(s) URL, so it is text too. Media holds the images and videos asked for, messages the rest: kinds of only images and videos leave messages null, and kinds with neither leave media null.

since.doc: Sent at or after this time.

until.doc: Sent before this time. since must be before until.

partial.doc: After the messages with every word, add those with some of them (partial is true on each). Left out is false.

SearchResult.doc: A section that wasn't asked for or didn't run is null; one that ran and found nothing is empty.

chats.doc: Chats in any place whose name matches (a DM also by the name of the person it is with): a name that begins with the first word first, then the newest message first.

in_groups.doc: People whose name matches, who are in a group with me and have no direct chat with me. Ordered as chats.

bookmarks.doc: Messages I bookmarked, of every kind, newest first. For empty text with no filters, the five newest bookmarks, newest bookmark first, with no next page.

messages.doc: Every other kind of message, newest first.

last_archived.doc: Only for empty text with no filters: the chat archived most recently, leaving out hidden chats and open_room_id. null otherwise, or when there is none.

complete.doc: false while older messages are still being added; results may be missing some.

hint.doc: emoji_only: the text has only emoji or punctuation, and nothing was searched. need_more_letters: under 2 letters, so media and messages didn't run (null) while chats and in_groups did.

PersonHit.doc: Someone found by name in a group I share with them.

room_id.doc: Their most recent shared group: the one with the newest message.

groups.doc: How many groups I share with them.

hits.doc: Newest first; with partial, every full match first.

next_cursor.doc: Pass as cursor for the next page. null when this is the last. A page may hold fewer than limit hits, to stay under 1 MiB: only next_cursor says whether there is more.

event_id.doc: Open the chat at it with room.events around.

place.doc: Where the chat is. A result outside the inbox says so.

sender_name.doc: The sender's display name, or the localpart of their ID when they have none.

snippet.doc: At most 160 characters of the message's text (as edited) around the first match, with … where it was cut.

ranges.doc: The matched words in snippet, in order.

media_path.doc: For an image or a video: its thumbnail (or the file itself), when the engine has it. "" otherwise.

view_once.doc: True when the matched message is view-once media (its media_path is blanked).

partial.doc: It matches some of the words, not all (filters.partial).

text.doc: What was typed, exactly: *, _, # and <b> are text, never formatting. At most 65,536 bytes of UTF-8; longer is -32602.

entities.doc: The text's formatting. Ranges that don't fit the text are -32602. The chat keeps the kinds its network keeps (ChatFeatures.formatting); the rest go as readable plain text.

reply_to.doc: The event_id of the message this replies to.

thread_root.doc: The root of the thread this goes in. -32023 where the chat has no threads (ChatFeatures.thread).

hold_ms.doc: Undo send: hold the message this long (ComposerPreferences.undoSendMillis), as queued, before it goes. One of 0, 750, 1000, 2000, 3000, 5000 and 10000 (any other is -32602); left out is 0, at once. Above 0 is part of a plan (-32022 when it isn't), and answers at once.

disable_link_preview.doc: Suppress outgoing link preview generation for this message.

path.doc: An absolute path to a regular file of at most 90 MB.

entities.doc: Taken and ignored: a file has no text.

SendStickerParams.doc: Send a sticker (m.sticker) from a local file path or existing media URL.

SendGIFParams.doc: Send an animated GIF or looping MP4 (m.room.message with fi.mau.gif: true).

TextEntity.doc: One formatting range of a message's text.

offset.doc: Where it starts, in UTF-16 code units, as NSRange counts them.

url.doc: For a link: http, https or mailto only.

user_id.doc: For a mention: a member's Matrix ID (room.members), or @room for everyone.

ChatFeatures.doc: What a person can do in one chat, as its network's bridge says. A greyed action says why from these, in Courier's words.

thread.doc: A reply in a thread (Reply in Thread, the thread pane).

reply_is_thread.doc: The chat has threads and no plain replies (Slack, WhatsApp community announcement groups): Reply is Reply in Thread.

edit.doc: My text messages can be edited.

edit_max_age_ms.doc: How old a message may be to be edited. 0 is no limit.

edit_max_count.doc: How many times one message may be edited. 0 is no limit.

unsend.doc: My messages can be deleted for everyone. false where the network only deletes for me (Google Messages).

unsend_max_age_ms.doc: How old a message may be to be unsent. 0 is no limit.

delete_reaches_phone.doc: Delete for Me also deletes it from the phone's own app (Google Messages).

current_timer.doc: The chat's disappearing timer now, which new messages get. null when it is off.

formatting.doc: The formatting the chat keeps. Other kinds go as plain text. [] keeps none.

mention_room.doc: @room reaches everyone (Slack). Elsewhere it is plain text.

max_text_length.doc: The longest text the engine sends, in bytes of UTF-8 (not characters): longer is -32602. A network with a shorter limit fails the message.

source.doc: Where these came from: the chat's stored features, the network asked because none were stored, or neither (only send, reply and Delete for Me).

can_set_name.doc: I can rename the group for everyone.

can_set_topic.doc: I can change the group's description for everyone.

can_set_avatar.doc: I can change the group's picture for everyone.

can_invite.doc: I can add people to the group.

can_kick.doc: I can remove people from the group.

can_set_admin.doc: I can make or dismiss admins in the group.

can_leave.doc: I can leave the group on its network.

can_delete.doc: I can delete the chat on its network.

delete_leaves_group.doc: Deleting this group chat on its network also leaves the group (WhatsApp).

location_supported.doc: Whether the chat supports sending location pins (m.location).

link_previews_supported.doc: Whether the chat supports outgoing link previews.

FileKindFeatures.doc: Per-kind file and media capabilities from a bridge's event.FileFeatures.

MediaCapFeature.doc: Sticker or GIF sending capabilities from a bridge's event.RoomFeatures.File map.

query.doc: What was typed after @. Each word, folded as search folds it (accents, case), must begin a word of the name. "" matches everyone.

Member.doc: Someone in the chat on its network: not me, nor the bridge's bot, nor anyone who left.

name.doc: Their name in the chat, else their profile's, else their ID's localpart.

type.doc: ChatFeatures.disappearing's type, or "" (with timer_ms 0) to turn it off.

timer_ms.doc: One of ChatFeatures.disappearing's timers_ms, or 0. Another is -32014.

room_ids.doc: 1 to 20 chats; a chat named twice gets one copy. More is -32602, and nothing is sent.

ForwardResult.doc: Each chat named, once: sent a copy, or not.

code.doc: The error that chat would have given alone: -32010, -32011, -32016, -32018 or -32020.

Draft.doc: What was typed, given back for the composer.

on.doc: Bookmark it, or take its bookmark away.

versions.doc: The message as first sent, then each edit of it that wasn't refused or deleted, oldest first.

formatted_body.doc: Its HTML. "" when it is plain.

due_at.doc: After now and at most 5 years ahead (else -32014).

condition.doc: if_no_reply: a message from someone else in the chat after it was set (or last changed) cancels it.

disable_link_preview.doc: Suppress outgoing link preview generation for this message.

ScheduledMessage.doc: A message scheduled to be sent later. It is in no chat's timeline, nor in search, until it is sent.

state.doc: waiting to go. canceled: someone replied first (if_no_reply). missed: due over an hour before the engine could send it; it waits for Send Now, a new time or Delete. A sent message is no longer listed.

set_at.doc: When it was scheduled or last changed.

scheduled.doc: Soonest first, in any state. At most what fits in 1 MiB: the soonest.

ScheduledUpdateParams.doc: Change what is given. Any change makes it waiting again, set now; a canceled or missed message needs a new due_at (else -32014).

due_at.doc: After now and at most 5 years ahead.

text.doc: A new text, with entities its ranges.

entities.doc: Without text: new ranges for the text it has.

options.doc: 2 to the chat's max_options, each 1 to its option_max_length characters, no two the same. Else -32014.

multiple.doc: A person may choose every option, or one.

option_ids.doc: 0 to the poll's max_selections of its option ids, each once (else -32014). [] takes my vote back.

typing.doc: true: I am typing (sent at the first change and every conventions.typing_repeat_ms while the text keeps changing). false: I stopped.

room_id.doc: The group the person is in.

network.doc: The network, when starting a chat without a shared group.

account_id.doc: The account on that network, when it has more than one.

user_id.doc: The person: a sender or member of that group, or a ghost on network.

Sent.doc: The event that was stored for what was sent. Its status changes come as changed notifications.

flow.doc: One of the account's flows. Left out or "" means its first.

another.doc: true: sign in beside the accounts linked, whatever state they are in (a second account).

account_id.doc: Sign this account (a Login's account_id) in again: only one in a state Reconnect fixes (LOGGED_OUT, BAD_CREDENTIALS, UNKNOWN_ERROR), else -32013. 1 to 256 bytes; one that is no account of the network's is -32602, and so is giving it with another true. With neither another nor account_id, the network's first account is signed in again when it needs it (else -32013), or the network's first account is added.

values.doc: For user_input, by field id; for cookies, by cookie field id. A cookies step leaves out a value it could not find.

LoginStep.doc: What the sign-in shows next. Optional keys are left out when empty.

login_id.doc: The sign-in session, for login.submit, login.wait and login.cancel. Not an account: that is account_id.

type.doc: display_and_wait: show display, then login.wait. user_input: ask for fields, then login.submit. cookies: sign in on a web page, collect cookies, then login.submit. complete: linked; the sign-in is over. unsupported: a step Courier can't do; instructions say what to do instead, and the sign-in is over.

remote_name.doc: On complete: what the network calls the account.

account_id.doc: On complete: the account the sign-in became (a Login's account_id).

other_account.doc: On complete, true when the sign-in became another account than the account_id login.start asked to sign in again (the person scanned with another phone, say). That account is kept as it was, still needing Reconnect, and the one signed in is added beside it; the app says so. Left out otherwise.

data.doc: The QR code's contents, the emoji or the code.

type.doc: password and token are secret: hide them as typed, and send them exactly as typed.

pattern.doc: A regular expression the value must match.

default_value.doc: What a blank answer means. The app may pre-fill it.

url.doc: The page to sign in on.

wait_for_url.doc: A pattern the page's address matches once the person has signed in.

extract_js.doc: A script that resolves to some or all of the values (the special source).

pattern.doc: A regular expression the URL-decoded value must match.

Changed.doc: Something the app shows has changed. Re-query it; the notification carries no data. kind room: a chat's row (name, picture, members, mute); with no room_id, names or pictures changed in chats unknown, so re-read the inbox and the open chat. event: a new event in room_id. status: event_id in room_id changed status, or was discarded. read: room_id's read marker moved. bridge: network's account changed state. spaces: labels, the spaces layout or an account's or label's space settings changed; no room_id, so re-read spaces.list (and the inbox, whose rows show labels). typing: who is typing in room_id changed. reminder: room_id's reminder fired, so tell the person (a room change for its row comes too). scheduled: room_id's scheduled messages changed (scheduled, changed, sent, canceled, missed or deleted), so re-read scheduled.list. receipt: someone's read receipt or a delivery arrived for a message in room_id, so re-read the open chat's page (read_by, delivered) and the chat's row (preview_status). resync: changes were lost because the app read too slowly, so re-read everything. It is sent once per loss, as soon as the app has read what was kept, even if nothing changes after it.

room_id.doc: On room (usually), event, status, read, typing, reminder, scheduled and receipt.

reason.doc: What is wrong, for people. It names the parameter (a key the method does not take, too), never its value.

refresh.doc: When true, refresh chat info from the bridge before answering.

event_id.doc: The message that shared the link.

name.doc: The effective display name (local_name when set, else remote_name).

remote_name.doc: The network's name for the chat.

local_name.doc: This Mac's local name override, or "".

topic.doc: The group topic or description, or "".

avatar_path.doc: Absolute path to the chat's avatar file on disk, or "".

local_avatar_uri.doc: This Mac's local avatar mxc:// URI override, or "".

is_direct.doc: True for a one-to-one chat, false for a group.

encrypted.doc: True when the chat is end-to-end encrypted.

disappearing_ms.doc: Current disappearing message timer in ms, or 0 when off.

pinned_event_ids.doc: Event IDs pinned in the chat.

shared_media.doc: Recent photos and videos shared in the chat.

shared_files.doc: Recent documents and files shared in the chat.

shared_links.doc: Recent links shared in the chat.

features.doc: Capabilities and admin permissions in this chat.

local_name.doc: Local name override on this Mac ("" clears it).

local_avatar_path.doc: Path or mxc:// URI for the local avatar override ("" clears it).

path.doc: Absolute file path chosen by the user in a save panel.

messages_written.doc: How many messages were written to the file.

room_id.doc: The chat to report as spam.

leave_or_delete.doc: When true, also leave the group or delete the 1:1 chat on the network when supported.

path.doc: File path to the new avatar image, or "" to clear.

user_id.doc: The member to promote or demote.

is_admin.doc: True to promote to admin, false to demote.

user_id.doc: Matrix user ID of the contact.

avatar_path.doc: Absolute path to the avatar file on disk, or "".

identifiers.doc: Phone numbers, emails or usernames for this contact.

room_id.doc: Existing or newly created 1:1 room ID with this contact, when present.

identifier.doc: Phone number, username or user ID.

start_chat.doc: When true, also create or open the 1:1 chat.

network.doc: Which network to create the group on.

text.doc: Personalized message text for this room.

messages.doc: Target 1:1 rooms and their personalized message text.

events.doc: The sent (or failed) event in each target room, in order. Failed events carry status_reason "not sent", "not connected", or "network_refused".

name.doc: Display name of the merged chat.

avatar_path.doc: Absolute path to the merged chat's avatar file on disk, or "".

last_room_id.doc: Default target room ID for sending in this merged chat.

networks.doc: Networks of the member rooms, in matching order.

created_ts.doc: When the merged chat was created (Unix ms).

name.doc: Display name for the merged chat.

room_ids.doc: Two or more 1:1 room IDs to combine.
Updated list of two or more member room IDs.

last_room_id.doc: Optional active room ID for the composer.

StickerItem.doc: A sticker, custom emoji, or recent GIF entry in the local catalog.

StickerPack.doc: A sticker or custom emoji pack from recent history, user imports, or a connected bridge.

refresh_bridge_packs.doc: When true, refresh sticker and custom emoji packs from connected bridges.

path.doc: Absolute path to a local .png, .webp, .gif, .apng, or .jpg file.

shortcode.doc: Optional custom emoji shortcode (surrounding colons are stripped).

usage.doc: Usage tags: sticker, emoticon, or both.

hello.doc: The handshake. It must come first.

accounts.list.doc: Every network the engine knows, the state of its account and each of the account's logins. It answers as soon as the engine is up, before every network has started (those are STARTING).

inbox.list.doc: One page of chats: a space, narrowed by filters, in a sort; or the chats room_ids names. Pages go by cursor, not by position, so in every sort a chat that doesn't move while you page is listed exactly once. A chat that moves between pages (a new message under oldest; a pin, an unpin or a reminder change under any sort) can be listed twice: keep the first and drop a later copy by room_id. A space_id that isn't one of the forms spaces.list gives, an unknown filter or sort, a cursor of another query, or room_ids with space, filters or sort is -32602. A well-formed space that doesn't exist (label:999, or an account with no chats) is not an error: it lists no chats.

spaces.list.doc: The spaces bar: built-in spaces, accounts and labels, in order, with their counts.

spaces.setLayout.doc: Save the bar's order and which spaces are hidden. A layout that doesn't start with inbox, names a space twice or hides inbox is -32014.

spaces.update.doc: Change an account's or a label's space settings. A built-in space has none (-32014).

labels.create.doc: Make a label. Its space joins the bar at the end.

labels.update.doc: Rename a label, or change its colour or icon.

labels.delete.doc: Delete a label. It comes off every chat, and its space and auto-archive rule go with it.

room.setPinned.doc: Pin or unpin a chat. Pinning brings it back from the archive. A network that takes pins (Account.syncs) is told too.

room.setArchived.doc: Archive or unarchive chats. A new message from someone else brings an archived chat back. A pinned chat is never archived: it is left out of room_ids, and when every chat named is pinned it is -32021.

room.setLowPriority.doc: Move chats to Low priority, or back. A new message leaves them there. Moving them there is part of a plan (-32022 when it isn't); moving them back always works.

room.setHidden.doc: Hide chats, or show them again. A new message leaves them hidden.

room.setMarkedUnread.doc: Mark chats unread, or clear the mark. The mark stays on this Mac: no network is told.

room.setLabel.doc: Put a label on chats, or take it off.

room.setDraft.doc: Keep the unsent text of a chat's composer. It stays on this Mac.

room.acceptRequest.doc: Accept a message request. The chat moves to the inbox, and the network is told. On a network that can't take an accept (Account.syncs has no accept_request) it is -32023 and nothing changes.

reminder.set.doc: Set, or replace, the reminder of chats. Part of a plan (-32022 when it isn't). A due_at not after now or more than 5 years ahead, or an unknown condition, is -32014.

reminder.clear.doc: End the reminders of chats, set or fired. A chat without one is no error.

inbox.archiveMatching.doc: Archive, all at once, the chats of a space that match: "Archive all read", "Archive older than a week". A built-in space other than inbox, or an older_than_ms that isn't one of the offered ages, is -32014.

inbox.markAllRead.doc: Mark read every unread chat the space lists (unread, or marked unread). Each network is told, as room.markRead tells it.

autoArchive.set.doc: Save a rule, new (rule_id 0) or changed, and answer it as stored. Part of a plan (-32022 when it isn't). A rule out of shape, a second enabled after_reply or after_read rule, or a second older_than rule for one space is -32014; an unknown rule_id or label is -32020. Changing a rule's duration moves the archives it has already scheduled; turning it off drops them.

autoArchive.delete.doc: Delete a rule, and the archives it had scheduled.

search.query.doc: Search this Mac's chats, people, bookmarks and messages. Answers don't change by themselves: run it again for newer results. A changed notification doesn't re-run a search. -32602's reason says what is wrong: text is too long, sections is not one of …, cursor needs exactly one of bookmarks, media or messages, cursor is not one this query handed out, limit must be 1 to N, since must be before until, unknown kind, network, sender or chat_type, room_ids must name 1 to 100 chats.

room.events.doc: One page of a chat's history, newest first: the newest page, the one older than before, the one newer than after, or the one around a message (to open the chat at a search result); or, with thread, one page of a thread. Paging out from any page with its before and after reads every event once.

room.markRead.doc: Mark a chat read up to its newest message. The unread count clears at once, and so do an unread mark and a reminder that has fired; the network is told when it can be (best effort).

room.setTyping.doc: Tell the chat's network I am typing, or that I stopped (conventions.typing_repeat_ms says when the app sends it). It answers at once and is best effort: a chat whose network isn't connected (not running, starting, or the chat's account logged out) is told nothing, and that is no error; nothing is kept for later. Only an unknown chat is refused.

room.setUnreadFrom.doc: Mark a chat unread from a message on (Mark as Unread on a message): its unread count runs from that message, mine or someone else's, until the chat is read. The mark stays on this Mac: no network is told. The chat is the message's. A note (a timer change, a call) is -32023.

room.directChat.doc: The one-to-one chat with a person in a group (Reply Privately), on the group's own account: Courier's own chat with them when it has one, with no network needed, else one the network makes. A one-to-one chat (there is nothing more private), an account that can't start chats, or a person the network can't reach is -32023; a person who isn't in the group as far as Courier knows is -32020. Making one needs the network: one that won't run this session is -32016, and one still starting, or whose account doesn't connect in time, is -32018.

room.setMuted.doc: Mute or unmute a chat. A network that takes mutes (Account.syncs) is told too.

message.send.doc: Send a text message, through the chat's own account. It answers once the network has taken it or refused it; the stored event's status says which. Held for undo send (hold_ms), it answers at once, queued. When the network is starting or down, or the chat's account isn't logged in yet, or the chat has messages waiting already, it answers at once, waiting: the message goes when the account is back, oldest first, and message.undo takes it back. A network that won't run this session is -32016, and one with no account at all -32010: nothing would ever send it.

message.sendFile.doc: Send a file. Images, videos and audio are sent as such, by their contents. hold_ms and thread_root as message.send, and like it, a network that is starting or down answers at once, waiting.

message.react.doc: React to a message. Reacting twice with one key sends it once and answers the first reaction's event_id.

message.retry.doc: Send a failed message again, as the same event. It goes back to pending; a message (not a reaction) whose network is starting or down, or whose chat has messages waiting, becomes waiting instead, and goes when the account is back, as a new one would. Anything else waits for the chat's account to connect, and is -32018, still failed, if it doesn't in time.

message.discard.doc: Delete a failed message from this device.

room.features.doc: What a person can do in a chat, and its disappearing timer now. Read it again on a room change.

room.members.doc: The people in a chat whose name matches, for a mention.

room.setDisappearing.doc: Set a chat's disappearing timer, or turn it off. The network is asked and waited on: only once it takes the change does the chat have it (a room change comes). A network that refuses it is -32023, and nothing changed.

message.edit.doc: Edit a text message of mine. The edit is pending until the network answers; one it refuses fails, and the message reads as before, in the chat and in search. Someone else's is -32026; not text, not sent, deleted, or a network that can't edit is -32023; past the chat's edit_max_age_ms or edit_max_count is -32024. Nothing is sent then.

message.unsend.doc: Delete a message (or reaction) of mine for everyone. It leaves the chat at once; the redaction (the Sent event) is pending until the network answers, and one it refuses brings the message back, in the chat, the inbox and search. Someone else's is -32026; a network that can't (Google Messages), or a held, unsent or deleted message, is -32023; older than unsend_max_age_ms is -32024, refused before anything is sent.

message.deleteForMe.doc: Delete anyone's message on this Mac only: it leaves the chat, the inbox and search, with no placeholder. Where delete_reaches_phone, the phone's own app is told too, best effort. A held message is -32023 (message.undo takes it back).

message.forward.doc: Send a copy of a message to chats, one at a time, as message.send would: no attribution, no reply or thread, each chat's own timer. A chat whose network isn't connected right now (linked but reconnecting) fails at once in ForwardResult.failed as -32018, without waiting for it. A message that can't be forwarded (a poll, a deleted message) is -32023 and nothing is sent.

message.undo.doc: Take back a held (queued) message before its window ends, or a waiting one before its network is back (Don't Send): it leaves the chat and search, and what was typed comes back. Once it has gone it is -32025. It needs no plan.

message.sendHeld.doc: Send held messages now, without waiting for their windows: a chat's, or every chat's.

message.setBookmarked.doc: Bookmark a message on this Mac, or take its bookmark away. A deleted message is -32020. A status change for it comes.

message.schedule.doc: Schedule a text message to be sent later. Part of a plan (-32022 when it isn't). It is rendered for the chat now, and again when changed. One due over an hour before the engine could send it waits as missed.

scheduled.list.doc: A chat's scheduled messages, or every chat's.

scheduled.update.doc: Change a scheduled message. It needs no plan: a lapsed one never strands a scheduled message.

scheduled.sendNow.doc: Send a scheduled message now, whatever its state. Its chat's network must be running and linked.

scheduled.delete.doc: Delete a scheduled message, whatever its state.

poll.create.doc: Start a poll in a chat that takes them (ChatFeatures.poll, else -32023). Everyone sees the results as they come in.

poll.vote.doc: Vote in a poll, replacing my earlier vote. An ended or deleted poll, or a chat that doesn't take polls, is -32023.

login.start.doc: Start signing in to a network: its first account, a second one beside it (another), or one of its accounts again (account_id). One sign-in per network at a time. A network still starting is -32016 until it runs.

login.submit.doc: Send what a user_input or cookies step asked for. A value that is refused is -32014, and the sign-in stays open for another try.

login.wait.doc: Wait for the phone to do what a display_and_wait step asked. It can take minutes.

login.cancel.doc: End a sign-in. It is harmless for one that is already over.

room.info.doc: Chat info inspector payload: metadata, encryption, disappearing timer, members, shared media/files/links, and capabilities.

room.setLocalOverride.doc: Set or clear a local display name or avatar override for a chat on this Mac only.

room.export.doc: Export a chat's text history to a local file chosen by the user.

room.reportSpam.doc: Report a chat as spam, hide it locally, and optionally leave or delete it on the network.

room.setName.doc: Change a group chat's name on the network.

room.setTopic.doc: Change a group chat's topic or description on the network.

room.setAvatar.doc: Change a group chat's avatar on the network.

room.invite.doc: Invite people to a group chat on the network.

room.kick.doc: Remove a member from a group chat on the network.

room.setAdmin.doc: Promote or demote a member as admin in a group chat on the network.

room.leave.doc: Leave a group chat on the network and hide it locally.

room.delete.doc: Delete a chat on the network when supported and hide it locally.

people.contacts.doc: List or search contacts from connected bridge accounts.

people.resolve.doc: Resolve an identifier (phone number, username, user ID) on a network and optionally start a 1:1 chat.

room.createGroup.doc: Create a new group chat on a network.

blast.send.doc: Send a text message independently to multiple 1:1 chats.

merge.create.doc: Combine two or more 1:1 chats into a local Merged Chat.

merge.update.doc: Update a Merged Chat's name, member rooms, or active sending room.

merge.delete.doc: Unmerge a Merged Chat, leaving its underlying 1:1 chats intact.

merge.list.doc: List all Merged Chats on this Mac.

merge.suggest.doc: Suggest unmerged 1:1 chats across networks that appear to be with the same person.

message.markPlayed.doc: Record that a voice note or view-once media item was played or opened on this Mac.

message.sendVoice.doc: Send a recorded voice note in a chat that supports voice messages.

message.sendLocation.doc: Send a geographic location pin (m.location) in a chat that supports location messages.

message.sendSticker.doc: Send a sticker (m.sticker) in a chat that supports stickers.

message.sendGIF.doc: Send an animated GIF or looping MP4 (fi.mau.gif) in a chat that supports GIFs.

stickers.list.doc: List recent, user-imported, and bridge-synced sticker and custom emoji packs plus recent GIFs.

stickers.import.doc: Import a local image file as a user sticker and/or custom emoji.

changed.doc: Sent by the engine after a successful hello, whenever something the app shows changes.

errors.doc: Every error has a code and a fixed message; neither the message nor data ever contains a value that was sent. The JSON-RPC codes (-32700, -32600, -32601, -32602, -32603) and -32002 can come from any request, and -32001 from hello. A method lists the others it can give.

codes.name: parse_error
codes.when: The line is not JSON. The id is null.

codes.name: invalid_request
codes.when: Not a JSON-RPC 2.0 request object.

codes.name: method_not_found
codes.when: No such method.

codes.name: invalid_params
codes.when: A parameter is missing, has the wrong type or is out of range, or names something the method doesn't know (an inbox.list filter, a cursor of another query, a search kind or network), or parameters that can't go together (room.events before, after and around; thread with around or after). Formatting ranges that don't fit the text (data.reason names entities), a text over 65,536 bytes (text), a hold_ms not offered, a forward to 0 or more than 20 chats, a login.start account_id that is no account of the network's (or given with another true). data says which.

codes.name: internal_error
codes.when: Something failed inside the engine.

codes.name: protocol_mismatch
codes.when: hello's protocol is not the engine's.

codes.name: hello_required
codes.when: A method other than hello before a successful hello.

codes.name: not_linked
codes.when: The chat's network has no account.

codes.name: bridge_command
codes.message: the bridge would run this as a command
codes.when: The text, or the file's name, starts with the network's bridge command prefix (!whatsapp, say). Nothing was sent.

codes.name: too_large
codes.message: the file is too large to send (the limit is 90 MB)
codes.when: message.sendFile with a file over 90 MB.

codes.name: already_linked
codes.when: login.start that would sign in again an account that works: the network's first account (neither another nor account_id), or the one account_id names. Only an account that is LOGGED_OUT, BAD_CREDENTIALS or UNKNOWN_ERROR can be signed in again; another signs in beside it instead.

codes.name: bad_value
codes.when: An unknown network or flow, a value the network won't take, or a call that does not fit the step (login.wait on a user_input step), and the sign-in stays open. Or a value the engine doesn't keep: a label title, colour or icon out of range, a draft too long, a reminder time that has passed, a spaces layout that moves or hides inbox, a rule out of shape.

codes.name: unknown_login
codes.message: no sign-in in progress with that ID
codes.when: The sign-in finished, was cancelled, timed out or never existed.

codes.name: not_running
codes.when: The network did not start this session (Telegram without its credentials, say), or has not started yet (its account is STARTING) for login.start and for every action that goes out through the network and isn't queued (an edit, a reaction, an unsend, a poll, a vote, a timer change, an accept). A new message is never refused while it starts (it waits), and room.directChat answers -32018 instead.

codes.name: login_in_progress
codes.message: a sign-in is already in progress for this network
codes.when: login.start while another sign-in on that network is live. Cancel it first.

codes.name: not_connected
codes.when: The chat's account is linked but did not connect in time, for an action that isn't queued (an edit, a reaction, an unsend, a poll, a vote, a timer change, a private chat to make): it would be wrong hours later. Also room.directChat while its network is still starting, when Courier has no one-to-one chat with the person to answer with. Nothing was sent. A new message is never refused this way: it waits.

codes.name: not_failed
codes.message: only a failed message can be retried or discarded
codes.when: message.retry or message.discard on a message that is pending or sent.

codes.name: not_found
codes.when: An unknown room_id, event_id or reply_to, or a message in another chat (room.events around, too); an unknown label_id, rule_id or label space; a search.query room_ids chat the engine doesn't have.

codes.name: pinned
codes.message: a pinned chat can't be archived
codes.when: room.setArchived when every chat it names is pinned. Unpin it first.

codes.name: not_entitled
codes.message: this isn't part of your plan
codes.when: A feature the person's plan doesn't include: reminders, Low priority, auto-archive rules, undo send (hold_ms above 0), send later. Nothing was changed.

codes.name: not_supported
codes.when: The chat's network can't do that (an accept, an unsend on Google Messages, a thread, a poll), the message can't (an edit of a photo, a forward of a poll, room.setUnreadFrom on a note), or the network refused a change the engine waits on (a disappearing timer). Nothing was changed.

codes.name: too_old
codes.message: that message is too old to change
codes.when: message.edit or message.unsend past the chat's edit_max_age_ms, edit_max_count or unsend_max_age_ms. Nothing was sent.

codes.name: already_sent
codes.when: message.undo on a message that is no longer held: its window ended, or it was sent now.

codes.name: not_yours
codes.message: you can only change your own messages
codes.when: message.edit or message.unsend on someone else's message.

codes.name: network_refused
codes.when: The network turned the change down (a rename, photo, description, add, remove, admin change, leave, delete or new group). Nothing changed on this Mac.

codes.name: needs_ffmpeg
codes.message: sending voice notes on this network needs ffmpeg
codes.when: message.sendVoice when the chat's bridge requires transcoding the recording into another container (such as Ogg/Opus) and ffmpeg is not installed on this Mac.
